issues.t: High-voltage battery can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some cars show a battery or EV system warning; in the worst case smoke or fire from under the car, sometimes while parked or charging.
issues.why: Some battery cells built by LG at one plant had a folded anode tab that could cause an internal short circuit. Hyundai first updated the battery software and later recalled these cars to replace the whole battery pack.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recalls 20V-630 and 21V-127. Until the new battery is installed, follow Hyundai's charging limits and park outside away from buildings.

issues.t: Coolant leak in the power electronics can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: A warning message and sudden loss of drive power, sometimes with code P0AA6.
issues.why: The housing of the electric power control unit (EPCU) was not sealed well enough, so coolant could leak inside and short the electronics.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-941. The dealer inspects the unit and replaces it if needed, for free.

issues.t: Engine damage from faulty piston oil rings (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking, oil burning, low oil, a flashing check engine light, loss of power, or the engine stalling. Oil can leak onto hot parts.
issues.why: Some oil control rings in the 2.0L engine were not heat-treated correctly. They can chip and scratch the cylinder walls, causing oil burning and engine damage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-301. The dealer installs engine-noise monitoring software, inspects the engine and replaces it if damaged, free.

issues.t: Dual-clutch shudder and hesitation at low speed
issues.sym: Shudder or jerking in first and second gear, a delay when pulling away, lurching in parking lots, and sometimes a transmission overheating warning in heavy traffic.
issues.why: The turbo Kona's 7-speed dual-clutch automatic uses dry clutches that are sensitive to heat and wear. Hyundai issued software updates and a bulletin for low-speed judder that can lead to clutch replacement.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest transmission software and a clutch check. Avoid creeping in traffic with light throttle, which heats the clutches.

issues.t: Key-start Konas are easy to steal
issues.sym: Signs of a theft attempt such as a broken steering column cover or damaged ignition, or the car being stolen.
issues.why: Konas started with a metal key have no engine immobilizer, and a widely shared method lets thieves start them quickly. Hyundai offers a software upgrade so the engine won't start unless the key fob unlocked the car. It may be covered.
issues.next: Have a Hyundai dealer install the anti-theft software upgrade, and consider a steering wheel lock. It may be covered.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump wear can cause power loss (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, rough idle, a loud misfire, and a check engine light, often at low speed.
issues.why: A valve inside the Kona N's high-pressure fuel pump can wear and let too much fuel through, making the engine run very rich.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-528. The dealer updates the engine software and replaces the pump if needed, free.

issues.t: Dual-clutch oil pump fault can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights and a fail-safe message, then after about 20–30 seconds the car loses drive power, even at speed.
issues.why: The high-pressure electric oil pump inside the Kona N's 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission can fault, and the fail-safe logic then disengages the clutches.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-746. The dealer inspects the transmission, replaces it if needed, and updates the software for free.

issues.t: Idle stop oil pump controller can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In rare cases smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, even when parked.
issues.why: The controller for the electric oil pump that keeps the transmission ready during engine auto-stop can have damaged electrical parts that overheat.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-526. Park outside and away from buildings until the dealer replaces the controller.

issues.t: 12-volt battery cable can short in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The positive battery cable can rub against a nearby bracket. In a frontal crash it could short and start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-901. The dealer adds protective sheathing for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not lock properly (recall)
issues.sym: A rear seat belt may not lock when tugged sharply, or may not retract normally.
issues.why: Some rear seat belt retractors were built incorrectly and may not hold an occupant in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-650. The dealer inspects and replaces the retractors as needed.

issues.t: EGR valve short can cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: A check engine light and a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: An internal short circuit in the exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve can make the engine lose power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-308. The dealer replaces the EGR valve for free.

issues.t: Rear center seat belt buckle may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: The rear middle seat belt may not latch firmly or may release.
issues.why: The rear center buckle may not restrain a passenger properly in a crash.
issues.next: Don't use the rear middle seat until the dealer replaces the buckle under recall 26V-452.

issues.t: Front steering knuckles may crack (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension, the car pulling, or loose steering. A broken knuckle can cause loss of steering control.
issues.why: A manufacturing error can leave the front steering knuckles prone to cracking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-069 and get the free inspection right away.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge screen goes dark while driving, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: A software error can make the instrument panel display fail.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for recall 26V-047. The update is free over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: AWD transfer case oil leak or burning smell
issues.sym: A hot oil or burning smell after driving, or oil drips near the front of the car on all-wheel-drive models.
issues.why: On 2.0L all-wheel-drive Konas the pinion oil seal in the transfer case can overheat and leak. Hyundai issued a bulletin for the leak and smell.
issues.next: Have the transfer case checked for leaks and the oil level topped off. Ask the dealer about bulletin 23-01-007H.

issues.t: Knock or rattle from the steering column
issues.sym: A knocking, rattling or clunking noise from the steering when turning or driving over rough roads.
issues.why: A bearing on the worm shaft in the electric power steering column can wear and get noisy. Hyundai issued several bulletins to replace the bearing or shaft.
issues.next: It is not usually dangerous, but have the dealer confirm the cause and apply the steering column bulletin.

issues.t: Blind spot warning shuts off
issues.sym: A message that blind spot collision warning is disabled, often in rain, snow or after a car wash.
issues.why: The rear radar sensors switch the system off when they think they are blocked or misaligned.
issues.next: Clean the rear bumper corners. If the warning keeps coming back in dry weather, have the radar sensors checked and aimed.

issues.t: Check engine light for cold-start misfire
issues.sym: A check engine light with misfire codes, usually set during a cold start and warm-up.
issues.why: Hyundai released an engine computer update because the misfire monitor could set codes during cold warm-up.
issues.next: Ask the dealer whether the software update (bulletin 20-FL-006H) has been done before replacing coils or plugs.

issues.t: Shifter sometimes won't come out of Park
issues.sym: With your foot on the brake, the shifter stays locked in Park now and then.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for some 6-speed automatic Konas that intermittently would not shift out of Park.
issues.next: Use the shift-lock release slot next to the shifter if you are stuck, and have the dealer apply the bulletin.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, a low oil warning comes on, or blue smoke appears from the exhaust.
issues.why: Owners report Konas burning oil heavily, sometimes leading to engine replacement. On 2.0L engines this is tied to the piston oil ring defect covered by recall 21V-301.
issues.next: Check the oil level every few fill-ups. Ask a dealer to check your VIN for open recalls and to run an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Fuel leak at the fuel pump
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the car near the rear seat area.
issues.why: Owners report fuel leaking from the fuel pump assembly on top of the tank.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Have it inspected right away and keep the car away from sparks or flames.

issues.t: Braking power can drop from a brake sensor fault (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light and a brake pedal that needs much more force to stop the car.
issues.why: The integrated electronic brake system in the Kona Electric could read an abnormal sensor signal and reduce braking power.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 20V-748 and get the free software update.

issues.t: Check EV system warning or battery won't fully charge
issues.sym: A 'Check electric vehicle system' warning, charging that stops early (for example at 50 percent), or reduced range.
issues.why: Faults in the battery management system, the onboard charger or the battery itself trigger these warnings. Hyundai has also issued several battery software updates.
issues.next: Have the dealer read the codes and install the latest battery software. The battery has an 8-year/100,000-mile warranty (10 years in some states).

issues.t: Whine, clunk or grinding from the electric drive unit
issues.sym: A whining, humming or grinding noise that changes with speed, or a clunk when switching between driving and regenerative braking.
issues.why: Owners report worn gears and bearings in the single-speed reduction gearbox and motor, and some cars have had the gearbox replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Record the noise and have the dealer check it while the car is under the powertrain warranty.

issues.t: 12-volt battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The car won't wake or turn on, the doors won't unlock electronically, or a low 12-volt battery warning comes on, even though the main battery is charged.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery that powers the car's computers can be drained by modules that don't fully go to sleep, and it is often a small, weak battery.
issues.next: Have the 12-volt battery tested and replaced if weak, and ask the dealer for a parasitic draw test and the latest software updates.

issues.t: Apple CarPlay or Android Auto drops out or the screen freezes
issues.sym: Phone projection disconnects, the screen goes black or freezes, or Bluetooth drops calls.
issues.why: Infotainment software bugs and USB connection faults are common. Hyundai issued bulletins for CarPlay software and for checking the USB and head unit.
issues.next: Try a different, high-quality cable and update the infotainment software. Ask the dealer about the CarPlay software bulletin.
